claims.text: High-entropy alloys possess intrinsic heterogeneous lattice distortions.
Heterogeneous lattice distortions modulate dislocation mobility.
Modulation of dislocation mobility enables reversible local strain localization during dynamic loading.
Reversible local strain localization enhances energy dissipation during dynamic loading.
The proposed as-cast initial alloy is well mixed.
The proposed as-cast initial alloy has high configurational entropy.
The proposed as-cast initial alloy has significant local lattice distortions.
Controlled annealing will partially reduce short-range compositional fluctuations.
Controlled annealing will reduce local lattice distortions.
Severe lattice distortions generate a spectrum of local stress fields.
The local stress fields cause reversible dislocation locking and unlocking during dynamic deformation.
Resistance to dislocation motion produces high strength.
Gradual activation of dislocation motion and associated energy dissipation produce ductility.
Annealing produces a more uniform but less dynamically adaptable dislocation response.
The as-cast alloy will have a higher dynamic modulus than the annealed alloy.
The as-cast alloy will have greater damping capacity and energy absorption than the annealed alloy.
The as-cast alloy will exhibit a more pronounced elastic-to-plastic transition than the annealed alloy under dynamic cyclic loading.
The proposed mechanism operates in single-phase, well-dispersed high-entropy alloys at moderate temperatures and strain rates.
The mechanism may cease to govern in multiphase alloys or under extreme conditions where other deformation mechanisms dominate.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome field identifies the annealed, less-distorted alloy as the baseline, whereas the baseline field identifies the as-cast, fully distorted alloy as the baseline.
